methodology: The synthesis of molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) based on ionic liquids was performed using ethylene glycol dimethacrylate as a copolymer matrix, with acrylamide as the template molecule and methacrylic acid or 2-(dimethylamino) ethyl methacrylate as comonomer. The MIPs were synthesized under conditions of polymerization in acetonitrile using propionamide as a monomer.
research_objective: The objective was to synthesize novel molecularly imprinted polymers based on ionic liquids for the selective extraction of acrylamide from solution, which is a contaminant present in some heat-treated foods such as soluble coffee extract.

key_findings.finding: MIPs based on ionic liquids show higher acrylamide binding capacity compared to non-imprinted polymers under similar conditions
The adsorption process follows a pseudo-first order rate mechanism, indicating that the maximum adsorption corresponds to a certain amount of acrylamide bound by the MIPs
Molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) based on 2-(dimethylammonium)ethyl methacrylate acetate (H-DMAEMA)[Ace] exhibit the highest adsorption capacity compared to non-imprinted polymers (NIP).
The formation of AM (alkyl ammonium monomers) is generated by heat-induced reactions involving the Maillard reaction.
AM can form covalent adducts with hemoglobin and nucleophilic DNA nitrogens, potentially leading to genotoxicity and carcinogenicity.
Development of polymeric materials for various applications including biocatalysis, lubrication and affinity-based sensing.
